$comment: Command templates for the quality eval. Each command is an argv array; {placeholders} are filled per call. Agent: {prompt} is the brief as a stranger would type it, {workspace} the empty directory the run starts in (also its cwd), {plugin} a freshly packaged copy of this checkout's plugin. Judge: {prompt} is the judging instruction, {packet} the directory holding only the brief, the rubric and the rendered pages (also its cwd), {schemaJson} the JSON schema the answer must match, inline on one line, {schemaPath} a file holding it where the caller has one, {schema} whichever of the two the judge's `schemaAs` names ("json", the default, or "path"), {model} the judge model. Entries marked `unverified` carry flags that were not checked against the installed CLI; confirm them with `<cli> --help` before trusting a run.

prompts.unattended:
{brief}

No one is available to answer questions during this run. Where you would ask, take the recommended default, say which in one line, and carry on to the delivered deck.

claude.note: Checked against `claude --help` (Claude Code): -p runs headless, --plugin-dir loads the packaged plugin (.claude-plugin/plugin.json) for this session only, --allowedTools grants file and shell access without prompts. The run has shell access in a temporary workspace; use a machine or sandbox where that is acceptable.

codex.unverified: The codex CLI was not installed where this template was written. `codex exec` is its headless mode; confirm the flags with `codex exec --help`. Codex loads the plugin from its installed marketplace entry rather than from {plugin}: package and install this checkout (python3 evals/scripts/package_plugin.py, then add it to the marketplace) before a run, or every run measures whatever version is installed.

claude.note: Read and Glob only, rooted at the packet. --json-schema makes the answer structured and takes the schema itself, not a file (checked against `claude --help`, Claude Code 2.1: a path is refused as not valid JSON); the runner also accepts a bare JSON object in the result text.
